_comment: The single place the native apps get their identity from. Read by capacitor.config.ts, by android/app/build.gradle, and by scripts/mobile-identity.mjs, so an identifier can never be right in one project and wrong in the other. NOT YET REGISTERED with either store — see `registered` below.
_appName_comment: The name that appears under the icon on a phone's home screen, and nowhere else. It is title-cased — Hangyul Ganada — because a launcher label sits beside Photos, Maps and Settings, and a lowercased second word reads there as a typo rather than as the deliberate lowercase of 가나다. The prose product name in the app, the store listing and every document stays `Hangyul ganada`; scripts/check-product-name.mjs enforces that split, and scripts/check-mobile-identity.mjs enforces that Android's strings.xml and iOS's Info.plist both carry exactly this value. Changing the name here and nowhere else is the supported way to rename the installed app.

registered._comment: Set each to true only once the identifier has actually been created in the corresponding console. Nothing in the build depends on these; they exist so the release checklist cannot be answered from memory.

_version_comment: 1.0.4 — the marketing version the release is published under. The tree carried 1.0.6 for one cycle (bumped from 1.0.5 for the child-safe content retirements) but nothing was ever uploaded under 1.0.5 or 1.0.6 — `registered` below is false for both stores and every build-info.json on record says so — so the number is free to be set to the intended one. A marketing version is a string the stores compare only against what they have already accepted, and they have accepted nothing. The build number is a different matter: see `_buildNumber_comment`. `scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs` holds every other copy to this value and `apps/web/src/config/product.test.ts` pins the literal 1.0.4 so a stray 1.0.6 cannot come back through any file.
_buildNumber_comment: 25, because 24 is spent. The delivered APK and AAB in result/ report versionCode 24 and product files change in this release (the launch screen, the quotation library, the daily-words answer reveal, the choice layouts, the copy). A code that has been used by a set of bytes is not reused for different bytes, and a marketing version going *down* from 1.0.6 to 1.0.4 changes nothing about that: Play orders builds by versionCode alone, so 1.0.4 at code 25 supersedes 1.0.6 at code 24. Never decrease this.

android._comment: targetSdk 36 because Google Play requires Android 16 for new apps and updates from 31 August 2026. minSdk 24 is Capacitor 8's floor and covers ~99% of active devices.

xcode._comment: What `App.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj` carries, written down here so that a check can tell a *deliberate lag* from a *drift*. For this release the two settings were moved in step with Android — MARKETING_VERSION 1.0.3 → 1.0.4 and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION 5 → 25, in both build configurations and touching nothing else in the project file — because the release requirement is one marketing version everywhere, and the store build number must stay ahead of every number ever used on either platform. `scripts/check-version-consistency.mjs` asserts the project file matches these two values exactly. The project file is otherwise Xcode-managed and no other setting in it is edited from Linux.
xcode.pending: None. iOS carries the same marketing version and build number as Android; the archive itself still has to be produced on macOS with Xcode — see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.

ios._comment: 15.0 to match IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET in the Xcode project — the two disagreeing is how a build succeeds and then crashes on a device the store said it supported. Capacitor 8's own floor is 14; 15 is chosen because it is what the project is configured for and covers every device Apple still updates. Apple requires builds made with the iOS 26 SDK from 28 April 2026; that is the SDK you build *with*, not the version you deploy *to*.
